title: Livingstone Stars With Bat and Ball but Super Giants Spoil London Spirit's Hundred Opener
excerpt: Liam Livingstone took 2-14 and smashed 69 off 40 balls in a superb all-round display, but Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker held their nerve at the death as Manchester Super Giants won by seven runs at Lord's.
body:
• Manchester Super Giants beat London Spirit by 7 runs in a thrilling men's Hundred contest at Lord's, with Gus Atkinson (2-15) and Sonny Baker (2-29) holding their nerve in the final 10 balls.
  • Liam Livingstone delivered a superb all-round performance for Spirit — taking 2-14 with the ball and scoring 69 off 40 balls — but was bowled by Baker with nine needed off four deliveries.
  • Tim Seifert struck 67 off 45 balls on his Hundred debut to anchor the Super Giants innings before a dramatic collapse of seven wickets for 33 runs.
  • Super Giants also won the women's match convincingly, with India's Smriti Mandhana and Richa Ghosh starring in a seven-wicket rout that was completed in just 59 balls.

Atkinson and Baker Hold Nerve in Dramatic Finish

Manchester Super Giants survived a Liam Livingstone masterclass to edge London Spirit by seven runs in a pulsating men's Hundred encounter at Lord's on Wednesday, delivering a double blow to the home side on their opening day of the 2026 competition.

https://x.com/thehundred/status/2080373986509173015

In front of a crowd of 23,847 — entertained between matches by a Tinie Tempah performance — Spirit were undone in both the women's and men's fixtures, according to Cricbuzz. But the men's contest was far from straightforward, with Livingstone turning in one of the finest all-round displays the tournament has seen.

Chasing 139, Spirit slumped to 51-3 inside the first 46 balls after losing Lhuan-dre Pretorius and James Rew cheaply. Livingstone, the Spirit captain, and South African Dewald Brevis pieced together a measured 68-run stand that hauled their side back into contention. With 56 needed off the last 30 balls, the contest was delicately poised.

Livingstone then took charge against Afghan spinner Noor Ahmad, smashing 12 off his final five deliveries including a trademark sweep over the leg side. A slog sweep for six brought up a 32-ball half-century before a drilled four through extra cover left Spirit within touching distance, CricketWorld reported.

With 21 required from the final 10 balls, however, England quick Atkinson delivered the decisive blow. Mixing his pace superbly, he dismissed Brevis with a sharp return catch to leave Spirit needing 12 off the final five deliveries. Fellow seamer Baker then produced the match-clinching moment, beating Livingstone with a full, rapid yorker that crashed into the stumps. Livingstone trudged off for 69 off 40 balls — an innings laced with five sixes — and Spirit's hopes went with him.

"It was a really good game of cricket, just a shame we fell short. It was never the plan to bowl 20 of the last 25 balls, but it came out nicely so I thought, whatever was working, just stick with it."

— Liam Livingstone, London Spirit captain

Seifert Sparkles Before Late Collapse

Earlier, New Zealand wicketkeeper Tim Seifert laid the platform for the Super Giants with a sparkling 67 off 45 deliveries on his Hundred debut. Opening alongside South Africa captain Aiden Markram, Seifert anchored the innings after a slow start and partnerships with Jos Buttler and Heinrich Klaasen guided the visitors to a commanding 105-2 after 67 balls.

What looked set to be a dominant total then unravelled spectacularly. Livingstone bowled 20 of the final 25 deliveries of the innings, returning figures of 2-14, while Australia leg-spinner Adam Zampa chipped in with 2-27. Spirit's bowlers triggered a collapse of seven wickets for just 33 runs, restricting Manchester to 138-9.

"We bowled some really good stuff through the middle, dragged it back towards the end, and we nearly chased it down. The stats don't tend to favour chasing here at Lord's, so it's a good start and something we can build on."

— Liam Livingstone

Mandhana and Ghosh Shine in Women's Rout

The day began with a comprehensive Super Giants victory in the women's match. India opener Smriti Mandhana and Australia's Meg Lanning put on a brisk 33-run opening stand before Spirit bowler Marizanne Kapp struck twice in two balls, according to Wisden. But India wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh settled the contest emphatically, blasting an unbeaten 15 off five balls as the Super Giants chased down Spirit's 80 in just 59 balls for the loss of three wickets.

Spirit's batting had earlier been woeful, with only Kapp's 17 off 12 — featuring two sixes — providing any resistance as they were bowled out for 80 off 91 deliveries. Sophie Ecclestone led the Super Giants' bowling attack in what was a one-sided affair.

What's Next

The double defeat leaves London Spirit bottom of both the men's and women's tables with zero points. For the Indian diaspora, the performances of Mandhana and Ghosh will be of particular interest as the Hundred continues to attract top Indian talent to English cricket's marquee franchise competition. The Super Giants, meanwhile, sit pretty after an opening-day clean sweep and face a busy schedule as the tournament heads into its second week.
